From 897d68d4ce7d50ca45a31e10c0e61597257b32d3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dmitry Baryshkov <dmitry.baryshkov@linaro.org>
Date: Fri, 29 Mar 2024 08:15:33 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] usb: typec: ucsi: allow non-partner GET_PDOS for Qualcomm
 devices

The name and description of the USB_NO_PARTNER_PDOS quirk specifies that
only retrieving PDOS of the attached device is crashing. Retrieving PDOS
of the UCSI device works. Fix the condition to limit the workaround only
to is_partner cases.

Fixes: 1d103d6af241 ("usb: typec: ucsi: fix UCSI on buggy Qualcomm devices")
Reviewed-by: Heikki Krogerus <heikki.krogerus@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Dmitry Baryshkov <dmitry.baryshkov@linaro.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240329-qcom-ucsi-fixes-v2-1-0f5d37ed04db@linaro.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c b/drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c
index f7157215eed6..29a7d71c9a40 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c
+++ b/drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c
@@ -619,7 +619,8 @@ static int ucsi_read_pdos(struct ucsi_connector *con,
 	u64 command;
 	int ret;
 
-	if (ucsi->quirks & UCSI_NO_PARTNER_PDOS)
+	if (is_partner &&
+	    ucsi->quirks & UCSI_NO_PARTNER_PDOS)
 		return 0;
 
 	command = UCSI_COMMAND(UCSI_GET_PDOS) | UCSI_CONNECTOR_NUMBER(con->num);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c`**
   - The condition that checks for the `UCSI_NO_PARTNER_PDOS` quirk has been modified. 
   - The original condition checked if the quirk was set without considering whether the device is a partner. The new condition now checks if the device is a partner (`is_partner`) before applying the quirk. 
   - This change ensures that the workaround for the quirk only applies to partner devices, allowing non-partner devices to retrieve PDOS without crashing.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `ucsi.c` directly addresses the issue described in the patch's description, which states that the quirk was incorrectly applied to non-partner devices. By refining the condition to check for `is_partner`, the patch resolves the bug while maintaining functionality for UCSI devices, thus improving the robustness of the code when handling different types of devices. This change is a targeted fix that enhances the existing functionality without introducing new issues.

Here is the commit message:
usb: typec: ucsi: allow non-partner GET_PDOS for Qualcomm
 devices

The name and description of the USB_NO_PARTNER_PDOS quirk specifies that
only retrieving PDOS of the attached device is crashing. Retrieving PDOS
of the UCSI device works. Fix the condition to limit the workaround only
to is_partner cases.

Fixes: 1d103d6af241 ("usb: typec: ucsi: fix UCSI on buggy Qualcomm devices")
Reviewed-by: Heikki Krogerus <heikki.krogerus@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Dmitry Baryshkov <dmitry.baryshkov@linaro.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240329-qcom-ucsi-fixes-v2-1-0f5d37ed04db@linaro.org
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the incorrect application of the `UCSI_NO_PARTNER_PDOS` quirk, which was preventing the retrieval of Power Data Objects (PDOS) for non-partner devices, leading to crashes. The condition did not properly check if the device was a partner before applying the quirk, resulting in unintended behavior when interacting with UCSI devices.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int ucsi_read_pdos(struct ucsi_connector *con,
 			  enum typec_role role, int is_partner,
 			  u32 *pdos, int offset, int num_pdos)
 {
 	struct ucsi *ucsi = con->ucsi;
 	u64 command;
 	int ret;
 
-	if (ucsi->quirks & UCSI_NO_PARTNER_PDOS)
+	if (is_partner &&
+	    ucsi->quirks & UCSI_NO_PARTNER_PDOS)
 		return 0;
 
 	command = UCSI_COMMAND(UCSI_GET_PDOS) | UCSI_CONNECTOR_NUMBER(con->num);
 	command |= UCSI_GET_PDOS_PARTNER_PDO(is_partner);
 	command |= UCSI_GET_PDOS_PDO_OFFSET(offset);
 	command |= UCSI_GET_PDOS_NUM_PDOS(num_pdos - 1);
 	command |= is_source(role) ? UCSI_GET_PDOS_SRC_PDOS : 0;
 	ret = ucsi_send_command(ucsi, command, pdos + offset,
 				num_pdos * sizeof(u32));
 	if (ret < 0 && ret != -ETIMEDOUT)
 		dev_err(ucsi->dev, "UCSI_GET_PDOS failed (%d)\n", ret);
 
 	return ret;
 }
